correctness.rationale: Exact k-cell multinomial mass admits a weighted Poisson expansion with first correction r_k(s) and O(n^-2) polynomially weighted error on every compact positive-intensity interval. For disjoint edges, r_4(s+t)-r_2(s)-r_2(t)=-(s-2lambda)(t-2lambda)/lambda exactly; independent Poisson score differentiation gives c=lambda mu_prime=2lambda exp(-2lambda) I0(2lambda). Variance equals (n-1)A+2(n-2)B+(n-2)(n-3)C, so A/B errors O(1/n) and C error O(1/n^2) prove n v(lambda)+O(1). The positive Hoeffding projection establishes strict positivity. The Poisson and Bessel expansions establish the claimed coefficient boundaries; numeric checker independently passed 90 assertions, including exact finite counting. No statement rests on numerics alone.

value.rationale: At N proportional to n the ordered histogram statistic responds to finite occupancies, so neither fixed-bin Gaussian asymptotics nor fixed-N sparse asymptotics is calibrated for it. Pairwise disjoint edge absolute contrasts have covariance only O(1/n), but their O(n²) multiplicity produces the order-n correction needed for the correct variance. The coefficient is explicit via a one-dimensional rapidly convergent Poisson series and a Bessel term, strictly positive, and has a sharp quadratic low-intensity boundary. This delivers a statistically motivated, nontrivial uniform variance law rather than a relabeled finite table; no downstream CLT or applied power improvement is claimed.
